title: The Missing Inheritance
premise: Silas Vasquez, the meticulous archivist of Saint Aldhelm's Cathedral, is drawn into the cold case of Marisol Ferro, a young woman who vanished from the cathedral grounds eleven years ago, leaving behind a diary whose entries continue past the date of her disappearance. As Silas decodes the diary's hidden references to the cathedral's sealed crypt, he realizes the killer is still alive, still watching, and using the case file itself to anticipate his every move. The trail leads to a survivor who has lived under a stolen identity for a decade, forced to bargain with the killer to stay alive. In the crypt beneath the cathedral, Silas confronts the true murderer—the cathedral's own beloved former verger—and saves the survivor, choosing truth over the institution's fragile loyalty.
about_author: Oscar Halloran is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing ecclesiastical records in northern England before turning to crime fiction. His novels are known for their claustrophobic settings and their obsession with what institutions bury to survive.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Silas Vasquez, POV. Silas catalogs the cathedral's restricted archive and establishes his pride: every case he touches, he closes. A visiting cold-case detective asks about Marisol Ferro's disappearance eleven years ago and the crypt sealed since before his tenure. The beat is quiet confidence laced with unease—the first crack in Silas's ordered world.

chapters.title: A Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The detective returns with Marisol's recovered diary; its final entries continue three weeks past her disappearance, in handwriting Silas verifies as authentic. Someone was writing as her—or she never vanished when they thought. The emotional beat is professional fascination curdling into dread as Silas accepts the case he may not be able to close.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Interleaved diary excerpts, Marisol's voice, with Silas's annotations. The post-disappearance entries describe the crypt, a bargain, and a name half-erased. Silas realizes the diary is addressed to whoever finds it—a message meant to survive its author. The beat is intimacy with a dead girl's voice and the vertigo of being watched through paper.

chapters.title: The Case File Knows Me
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas pulls the original investigation file and finds pages annotated in fresh ink—corrections to the investigators' mistakes, made recently. Someone with archive access has been tending this case for years. The beat is paranoia: the killer isn't hiding from the record; the killer is maintaining it.

chapters.title: What the Verger Kept
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas interviews Father Anselm and the aging staff, learning the crypt was sealed after a fire the year before Marisol vanished. The beloved former verger, Edmund Locke, retired abruptly and still lives in the close. Locke is warm, helpful, unsettlingly well-informed about Silas's progress. The beat is charm masking menace.

chapters.title: The Survivor's Bargain
chapters.summary: New POV: Elena Ruiz, a quiet bookbinder in the cathedral shop. Elena reads Marisol's name in the news and burns a letter she's kept for eleven years. Flashback fragments reveal she knew Marisol, and that someone forced her silence in exchange for a new identity. The beat is guilt sharpened into terror that the bargain is expiring.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The diary's marginal marks map to the cathedral's liturgical calendar—dates of services, times the crypt was unwatched. Silas reconstructs Marisol's final weeks and finds a second set of handwriting beneath hers: coaching, correcting, controlling. The beat is the thrill of decryption shadowed by the realization that Marisol was never alone in her own diary.

chapters.title: A Name Half-Erased
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Following the half-erased name, Silas finds a baptismal record altered decades ago—an identity manufactured inside the cathedral's own books. He suspects the diary's second hand belongs to someone still on the staff. The beat is betrayal: the institution he serves has been an accomplice all along.

chapters.title: Elena's Hands
chapters.summary: Elena, POV. Elena repairs an antique missal and finds a pressed flower—Marisol's—marking a page about the crypt. Locke appears at her workbench, courteous, asking what she remembers about 'that poor girl.' Elena lies well, because she has practiced for eleven years. The beat is a duel of courtesies with a knife beneath.

chapters.title: The Fire That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas digs into the crypt fire and finds the insurance report contradicts the diocesan account: nothing burned; the crypt was sealed to hide what was inside. Among the sealed contents, records hint at a death predating Marisol's disappearance. The beat is the price of survival made institutional—the cathedral buried truth to keep its doors open.

chapters.title: Someone Reads Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas's own working notes are disturbed; a page he left locked is annotated with a correction in the same fresh ink as the case file. The killer is inside his process, using the archive against the archivist. The beat is violation and a cold clarity: to catch the killer, Silas must feed the file a lie.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Record
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas plants a false entry in the case file—a fabricated lead placing evidence in the crypt—known only to three people. He watches which of them moves. Meanwhile the diary's last legible entry names the crypt's 'keeper' and promises the truth 'sleeps below.' The beat is the hunter becoming bait, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Elena Breaks
chapters.summary: Elena, POV. Locke confronts Elena with proof of her stolen identity, demanding she retrieve and destroy the diary before the archivist decodes it. Elena, cornered, agrees—but secretly copies a page first and leaves it where Silas will find it. The beat is loyalty to a dead friend outweighing the instinct to survive.

chapters.title: The Page She Left
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas finds Elena's copied page: a confession fragment implicating Locke in a death inside the crypt the year before Marisol vanished—and revealing Marisol discovered it. Silas realizes the 'missing person' was murdered to protect a secret the cathedral helped bury. The beat is grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Interview with a Verger
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas visits Locke, ostensibly about archive donations, and lets him see the false file entry. Locke's mask slips for a single sentence—too precise, too knowing. Walking away, Silas understands the trap worked and that Locke now believes the crypt must be opened tonight. The beat is dread and momentum: the endgame has a date.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Elena, POV. Elena, sent by Locke to unlock the crypt door, instead warns Silas, confessing her eleven years of complicity and the identity the cathedral gave her in exchange for silence. Silas must decide whether to use her or protect her. The beat is the theme made flesh: loyalty versus truth, and what each one costs.

chapters.title: Below the Cathedral
chapters.summary: Silas and Elena, alternating POV. At night they descend into the crypt ahead of Locke and find Marisol's remains arranged with terrible care—alongside a second, older skeleton and a box of records proving decades of buried deaths. Locke's footsteps sound above them. The beat is claustrophobic horror and the weight of every secret at once.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Crypt
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Locke seals them in and speaks through the door—calm, paternal, explaining that everything he did was to protect the cathedral and the people who loved it, Marisol included, 'as much as anyone can be protected.' The beat is the killer's terrible sincerity: he believes he is the loyal one.

chapters.title: The Diary's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Trapped with Marisol's remains, Silas finds the diary's true final page hidden in the crypt itself—Marisol's own hand, naming Locke and begging whoever finds it to tell the truth even if it costs the cathedral everything. Silas records evidence by phone light as Locke works to open the door. The beat is a dead girl's voice finally heard.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Dark
chapters.summary: Silas and Elena, POV. Locke enters; Silas stalls him with the one thing he cannot bear—the truth that his 'protection' destroyed the cathedral he loved, while Elena triggers the alarm Silas wired to the crypt bell. Police descend; Locke, unresisting, asks only to lock the crypt behind him one last time. The beat is climax: violence averted, evil unmasked, grief everywhere.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. In the aftermath, the diocese offers to bury the findings quietly; Silas refuses, releasing Marisol's full diary and Elena's testimony at the cost of his position and the institution's goodwill. Elena surrenders her false identity and begins reclaiming her real name. The beat is costly resolution: truth chosen, and paid for.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Silas, POV, months later. Silas, demoted but unbowed, files the completed case—every page annotated in his own hand, nothing erased—and locks the crypt with a new public record of what lies inside. Marisol is buried under her own name. The beat is quiet peace: the archivist closes the one case that changed what closing a case means.
